readings: Asynchronous reset dominates: areset is a level-sensitive asynchronous trigger, so q becomes 0 immediately when areset=1, independent of clk, and clk edges are ignored while areset=1.
Only posedge clk triggers the DFFs: areset is sampled on posedge clk, so q becomes 0 only at a clock edge when areset=1 (synchronous reset).
Asynchronous deassertion: when areset goes low, the DFFs are released immediately; if areset goes low before a posedge clk, q updates to d on the next posedge clk.

Synchronous deassertion: the reset is released only after the next posedge clk (e.g., via a reset synchronizer), so q remains 0 for one additional clock cycle after areset goes low before updating to d.
q initializes to 0 at power-up (implicit initial value), even before areset is asserted.
q is undefined (X in simulation) until areset is asserted at least once; no power-on reset value is implied.
